name: Asked In
tagline: Nobody had to let you. It was good before they did.
epigraph: Before anyone made it legally, a king's chamberlain was looking everywhere for whisky from this glen.
glassware: a small tumbler, one large ice cube
language_row: Wren's resonance: ready (v2; reaffirmed on v3 in r6). Guest text 4-gram clean against every pour (Wren r4–r5). Gendered pronouns in y1–y4 refer to George Smith, the Duke of Gordon and Grant's father only, accepted by Wren and Hester.
sources: Fact card `_studio/fact-cards/george-smith-glenlivet.md`: *The Oxford Companion to Spirits and Cocktails* (GLENLIVET pdf 917–918; SPIRITS MEASURE pdf 1878–1879; SCOTLAND AND IRELAND pdf 1768–1769; WHISKY pdf 2132; EXCISE pdf 752); Elizabeth Grant of Rothiemurchus, *Memoirs of a Highland Lady* (John Murray, 1898), p. 373; Phil Dwyer, *The Whiskey Wash*, 20 Mar 2025 (tasting notes). Drink: *Cocktail Codex* pp. 3, 5, 6, 175, 203–204; *The Flavor Matrix* (pdf 136). Room notes `work/outlaw-creator/`.
names_note: Asked In (Wren; the room's pick, all three, r5–r6). Also considered: Let In, Before They Did (spends the tagline twice), Made First, Mild as Milk (captions the drink), The Real One (Hester; "the real one" already appears in *Everybody's* and *On One Condition*).
open_items: Spark: elderflower liqueur (a style; St-Germain as the Codex's reference bottle, p. 175), turning up the 12's own "elegant and floral" (Codex p. 204). Passion fruit had a page (Dwyer) but went OUT on acid (0.10%) and, per Wren, a surprise is a statement. Honey dropped: already in the bottle and in *Any Day*. The Flavor Matrix grain entry (pdf 136) consulted and set aside.
Elderflower liqueur sugar and the substitute malt's strength are unsourced; Tomás swept both (sugar 6.62–8.10 g, ABV 27.4–31.0%), all in range.
Grant's whisky is the glen's, never Smith's; the illicit spirit is never called a single malt; no line calls today's bottle "his whisky" or states "unpeated" of it.
Kept out on purpose: the distillery's present owner and sales rank, the 1884 court order, Usher's 1853 vatting, pistols and fire, any "sell-out".
